A fisher wants to check the situation on the hook, so he rotates the fishing rod $AC$ to the position $AC'$. At this time, the length of the fishing line $B'C'$ exposed above the water surface is $8\mathrm{m}$. What is the length of $BB'$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Given $AC=10\text{ m}$, $BC=6\text{ m}$, and $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, \\ $AB=\sqrt{AC^2-BC^2}=\sqrt{10^2-6^2}=8\text{ m}$, \\ Given $AC'=10\text{ m}$, $B'C'=8\text{ m}$, and $\angle AB'C'=90^\circ$, \\ $AB'=\sqrt{AC'^2-B'C'^2}=\sqrt{10^2-8^2}=6\text{ m}$, \\ therefore $BB'=AB-AB'=\boxed{2}\text{ m}$.

Image description: In the figure, A is on the left, B' and B are located on the same horizontal water surface line, and B' is between A and B. Line segments B'C' and BC both go vertically upward from the water surface, connecting respectively to C' and C; line segments AC and AC' represent the two positions of the fishing rod. Therefore, △ABC is a right triangle at B, and △AB'C' is a right triangle at B'.
Reasoning: The fishing rod only rotates, so AC=AC'=10 m. Given BC=6 m, in right triangle ABC, AB=sqrt(AC^2-BC^2)=sqrt(10^2-6^2)=sqrt(64)=8 m. Also given B'C'=8 m, in right triangle AB'C', AB'=sqrt(AC'^2-B'C'^2)=sqrt(10^2-8^2)=sqrt(36)=6 m. Since A, B', B are collinear and B' is between A and B, BB'=AB-AB'=8-6=2 m.
